frbus_residuals._series_comment: series is the row's KIND of comparison, not a decoration: 1 = ours against the Fed's implementation under shock (the evidence), 2 = the Fed's own two releases against each other (the reference-noise yardstick our rows are judged against), 3 = a tracking identity that re-solves to its own input and therefore cannot fail. Series 3 was previously 1 on the first row, which painted the row the page calls 'not evidence' in the accent colour.

rows.label: ours vs LONGBASE — tracking identity, not evidence
rows.note: init_trac defines add-factors as minus the residuals at the input data, so re-solving reproduces it up to float64 for ANY input — verified: the same test passes at 6.7e-9 on randomly scrambled data. Shown for completeness; it measures arithmetic, not economics.

rows.label: pyfrbus 1.1.1 vs 1.0.0 — the Fed’s own releases

define_emissions._comment: What the define-uk divergence gate actually pins is the RATIO of the pinned run to the manual's Table 4, not the two levels: the levels in validation/figures/data/define_emissions_divergence.csv are rounded to whole MtCO2e, so recomputing the percentage from them gives -3.4 / -10.2 / -23.1 where the gate and the validation page say -3.5 / -10.2 / -23.3. The bars plot the rounded levels; the percentages come from the gated ratios below.
